concept.title: MCP Server Integration
concept.shortdesc: DITA Craft exposes its DITA intelligence — validation, key space resolution, context snapshots, and map analysis — to external AI agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

section.title: Overview
section.p: The MCP server lets AI coding agents like opencode, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Continue read and query your DITA workspace. It runs as a standalone Node.js process with no VS Code dependency — agents spawn it directly via stdio.
The server exposes 6 tools and 3 resources:

strow.stentry: Validate a DITA file or XML fragment and return diagnostics with error counts and severity
Token-budgeted map snapshot for LLM prompt injection (Levels 1/2/3)
List all defined keys and their resolved targets with scope and provenance filters
Return map topic hierarchy as JSON, tree text, or CSV
Resolve href, keyref, conref, or conkeyref to target file and element
Step-by-step key resolution trace with scope and keyref chain details

section.title: Building the MCP Server
section.p: Run the standalone build command from the DITA Craft project root:
section.codeblock: npm run build-standalone # → dist/mcp-server.js (3.2 MB) # → dist/lsp-server.js (2.0 MB)
section.p: Both bundles are self-contained — no node_modules needed at runtime.

section.title: Configuring the MCP Server
section.p: The server validates as the extension does in the same workspace: at startup it reads the ditacraft.* settings of .vscode/settings.json in the workspace, if the file exists. Comments and trailing commas are allowed, as in VS Code. Path settings (ditacraft.xmlCatalogPath, ditacraft.customRulesFile, ditacraft.rngSchemaPath) may be relative to the workspace or start with ${workspaceFolder}. Settings that only concern the editor, such as ditacraft.autoValidate, are ignored.
Environment variables, set in the agent's MCP configuration:

strow.stentry: Required. The DITA project folder. A relative path is taken from the server's working directory.
A settings file to read instead of .vscode/settings.json.
The custom rules file, overriding ditacraft.customRulesFile.
debug, info, warn (default) or error. At info, the log names the settings file and the catalog used.

section.note: As in the extension, ditacraft.xmlCatalogPath replaces the bundled DITA catalog: the catalog must also resolve the OASIS public identifiers that the project shells use, as the catalog of a DITA-OT installation (catalog-dita.xml) does.
section.p: Results always reflect the files on disk: a file is validated again on every request, and the maps changed since the previous request are read again, so keys and subject scheme values added to a map are seen at once.

section.title: Standalone LSP Server
section.p: DITA Craft also ships a standalone LSP server bundle for embedding in other Node.js projects:
Set the DITACRAFT_EXTENSION_ROOT environment variable to point to the directory containing the dtds/ folder. The LSP server uses stdin/stdout for JSON-RPC communication.

section.title: Workspace Security
section.p: The MCP server enforces workspace isolation:

ul.li: All file paths are resolved relative to the WORKSPACE folder
Path traversal attacks (../../ beyond 8 levels) are rejected
HTTP URLs, UNC paths, and null bytes are rejected
No document content is ever transmitted to external services

section.note: The MCP server uses stdio transport by default, which means all communication stays local to the machine. No network configuration is required.
